questions.question_text: Write $36$ minutes as a decimal number of hours.

options.why: Treats minutes as hundredths of an hour instead of dividing by 60.
Uses the 24-minute complement rather than the stated 36 minutes.
Divides $60$ by $36$ instead of dividing $36$ by $60$.

questions.question_text: Write $2$ hours $48$ minutes as a decimal number of hours.

options.why: Writes the minute digits after the decimal point instead of dividing by 60.
Uses 36 minutes as 0.6 hour instead of converting the stated 48 minutes.
Converts the minutes correctly but omits the two whole hours.

questions.question_text: Write $3.45$ hours as hours and minutes.

options.why: Reads the decimal digits directly as minutes instead of multiplying by 60.
Uses 0.3 hour for the minute part instead of the stated 0.45 hour.
Converts $0.45$ hour to $27$ minutes but omits the $3$ whole hours.

questions.question_text: Which interval is equal to $1.25$ hours?

options.why: Treats 0.25 hour as 25 minutes rather than one quarter of 60 minutes.
Treats 0.25 hour as one third of an hour rather than one quarter.
Uses three quarters of an hour instead of one quarter.

questions.question_text: Write $2.425$ hours as hours, minutes and seconds.

options.why: Multiplies $0.425$ by $100$ instead of $60$, giving $42.5$ minutes, then converts the half-minute to $30$ seconds.
Finds $25.5$ minutes but reads the decimal digit as $5$ seconds instead of multiplying $0.5$ by $60$.

questions.solution_text:
$0.425\times60=25.5\text{ min}$
$0.5\times60=30\text{ s}$
$2.425\text{ h}=2\text{ h }25\text{ min }30\text{ s}$

questions.question_text: Write $1$ hour $51$ minutes as a decimal number of hours.

options.why: Writes the minute digits directly after the decimal point instead of dividing by 60.
Reverses the digits of the minute value before treating them as hundredths.
Converts the 51 minutes correctly but omits the one whole hour.
